Independent decision-making – Analyze requirements and constraints discussed in meetings and independently determine the best course of action for cloud implementations. Documentation and knowledge sharing – Document designs, deployment processes, and configurations for the solutions you build. Familiarity with source control (Git) and template repositories for managing IaC. Azure DevOps & CI/CD – Proficiency with Azure DevOps (or similar CI/CD platforms) for automating build and release pipelines. Experience building CI/CD pipelines that deploy Azure resources using IaC (Bicep/ARM) and integrating automated tests or validations. Scripting and Automation – Strong scripting skills in PowerShell, Azure CLI, or Python for automation of routine tasks and custom deployment needs. Ability to write scripts to handle Azure service management, monitoring, and automation beyond IaC templates. Troubleshooting and Optimization – Ability to troubleshoot Azure environment issues (networking, performance bottlenecks, deployment failures) and perform root-cause analysis. Experience with monitoring tools and diagnostics to optimize performance and costs. Security & Networking Knowledge – Good understanding of Azure security (NSGs, IAM, Key Vault, etc.) and networking concepts (VNETs, subnets, VPN/ExpressRoute, DNS) in a cloud context. Capable of designing with security and compliance in mind. DevOps and Agile Principles – Experience working in an Agile environment and applying DevOps practices. Comfortable use of infrastructure automation tools and configuration management. Knowledge of containerization (Azure Functions) is a plus, though not required. Certification – Microsoft Azure Associate-level certification is required (e.g., Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) or Azure Developer Associate (AZ-204)). Higher-level or additional Azure certifications (Azure Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer Expert) are a plus. Proven track record of executing projects in a cloud environment.
